understanding.emotion: quietly lonely and carrying a secret
understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call not feeling good enough, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from carrying the secret and the quiet house to standing in the truth of what happened, with the footing to face your parents when you choose.

week_beats.hook: You recognise being left, and the loneliness of a quiet house you are not allowed to name.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that the secret and the quiet are not your size, and that the only harm is letting their picture replace your own.

understanding.core_struggle: A mother separated from her partner, seeing her children three nights a week, carrying the quiet house and the secret from her parents in Chandigarh.
understanding.mirror: You see your children three nights a week, and on the other nights the house is quiet and the television is on.
understanding.insight: The separation was done to you, and the quiet house is real. The secret from your parents is what you are carrying alone, and it is not your size.

queries.hook: Being left by the person who was meant to stay, and the loneliness of a quiet house you are not allowed to name to the people who raised you.
queries.diagnose: When others see only a role, their picture is their smallness and not your measure; the harm deepens only when their picture begins to replace your own.
queries.steady: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; your worth was never theirs to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.
queries.act: Speak the true thing gently and firmly when you are ready, hold your ground on what is yours, and do your own duty without shrinking to fit the picture they hold.
queries.story: A woman left by her husband, carrying her children alone, who stood in her truth before her family and found her footing without their approval.

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, who has collapsed in tears on the battlefield and refuses to fight.
verse.sanskrit: न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद्यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम् । अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धम्राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम् ॥
verse.line: Even winning everything wouldn't touch this grief that's drying me up inside.
verse.translation: I see nothing that could drive away this sorrow that is drying up my senses, not even an unrivalled, prosperous kingdom on earth or rule over the gods.
verse.why: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

prasang.title: Krishna and Arjuna on Arjuna's faint-heartedness
prasang.summary: Krishna challenges Arjuna's despair. Arjuna admits he is confused about what is right, cannot tell which choice is better, and asks Krishna to teach him.
prasang.lesson: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

verse.meaning: Arjuna has collapsed on the battlefield. He looks at Krishna and says that even if he won everything, even the rule of the gods, it would not touch this grief. He is drying up inside. He admits he cannot see a way out. He asks Krishna to teach him what to do next. The verse is an admission of confusion. It says that clarity begins when you admit you do not know and ask for help.
verse.for_you: You are in a quiet house that feels too big, holding a secret from your parents. You do not have to fix this alone right now. You can simply name what is happening to you, exactly as it is, without explaining it away.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Right after naming the five causes of any action, Krishna warns about the person who ignores four of them.
verse.sanskrit: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः । पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः ॥
verse.line: If you think you alone made it happen, or alone made it fail, you're not seeing the whole picture.
verse.translation: That being so, whoever, through an untrained understanding, sees himself alone as the doer does not truly see.
verse.why: You are one cause among five; own your part, not the whole outcome.
verse.misuse: Not a way to dodge responsibility; you are still one of the five causes.

prasang.title: What makes an action happen
prasang.summary: Every action has five causes: the setting, the doer, the instruments, the efforts, and providence. Seeing oneself as the only doer is a mistake.
prasang.lesson: You are one cause among five; own your part, not the whole outcome.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield. They have been told to act, but they are frozen by the weight of the war. Krishna explains that every action has five causes: the setting, the doer, the tools, the effort, and providence. Seeing oneself as the single cause of an outcome is a mistake of an untrained mind. The verse proposes that you are one cause among many. Your part is real, but it is not the whole picture.
verse.for_you: The quiet house and the secret from your parents are not your size alone. Your part in the separation is one of five causes. Let the picture of being the sole reason go, and make room for the truth that you are not the whole weight.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verse.sanskrit: जितात्मनः प्रशान्तस्य परमात्मा समाहितः । शीतोष्णसुखदुःखेषु तथा मानापमानयोः ॥
verse.line: Self-mastered and calm, you stay centred in heat and cold, pleasure and pain, praise and insult.
verse.translation: For one who has conquered himself and is at peace, the higher self stays steady in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, honour and dishonour.
verse.why: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.
verse.misuse: Staying steady under insult is not accepting mistreatment; you can stay calm and still speak up.

prasang.title: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

verse.meaning: Krishna continues to Arjuna about the self-mastered person. They have explained that the self can be a friend or an enemy. Now they describe the marks of the realised: they lift themselves by themselves. This person stays steady through heat and cold, pleasure and pain, praise and insult. They see friend and foe alike. The verse proposes that you can be your own best friend by choosing to stay centred.
verse.for_you: You can be your own friend while the house is quiet. Stay steady in the heat of the secret and the cold of the empty rooms. You do not have to accept the story that you failed. You can simply choose to stand in the centre.

verse.speaker: Ram
verse.setting: Ram has lain on the shore for three days asking the ocean for a way across. No answer comes.
verse.sanskrit: अवलेपः समुद्रस्य न दर्शयति यः स्वयम्। प्रशमश्च क्षमा चैव आर्जवं प्रियवादिता॥ असामर्थ्यफला ह्येते निर्गुणेषु सतां गुणाः।
verse.line: Calm, patience, honesty and kind words: people who don't value them will read them as weakness.
verse.translation: See the ocean's arrogance: he does not even show himself. Calm, forbearance, straightforwardness and gentle speech, these virtues of the good, are taken by the unworthy as signs of weakness.
verse.why: Be humble first. When humility is taken for weakness, act firmly, and stop once you're heard.
verse.misuse: Firmness only after real patience, and only toward someone who keeps ignoring you. When the ocean finally came, Ram listened and redirected the arrow.

prasang.title: Ram at the ocean: humble first, firm after
prasang.summary: Ram lies on kusha grass by the shore for three days, asking the ocean for a way. Ignored, he tells Lakshman that patience is being taken for weakness and takes up his bow. The ocean rises, offers a way (Nala's bridge), and Ram releases the arrow elsewhere at its request.
prasang.story_hook: For three days the prince lay on a bed of grass at the edge of the sea, asking politely.
prasang.lesson: Be humble first. When humility is taken for weakness, act firmly, and stop once you're heard.

verse.meaning: Ram lies on the shore, asking the ocean for a way across. No answer comes. He tells Lakshman that patience is being taken for weakness. He takes up his bow. The ocean rises, offers a way, and Ram releases his arrow elsewhere at its request. The verse says that when humble people speak calmly, those who do not value them read it as weakness. It asks you to be humble first, and only act firmly when your patience is ignored.
verse.for_you: The quiet house teaches you this. Your parents in Chandigarh have not answered your call. That silence is not your fault. You do not need to lower your voice. You could hold the truth of the separation in your own chest, and let them see it when you are ready.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.setting: From the section on helping others: how the good behave.
verse.sanskrit: तृष्णां छिन्धि भज क्षमां जहि मदं पापे रतिं मा कृथाः सत्यं ब्रूह्यनुयाहि साधुपदवीं सेवस्व विद्वज्जनम् । मान्यान् मानय विद्विषोऽप्यनुनय प्रख्यापय प्रश्रयं कीर्तिं पालय दुःखिते कुरु दयामेतत् सतां चेष्टितम् ॥
verse.line: Cut craving, forgive, drop arrogance, speak truth, win over even enemies, be kind to those suffering.
verse.translation: Cut off craving, practise forbearance, give up arrogance, take no delight in wrong, speak the truth, follow the path of the good, serve the wise, honour those worthy of honour, win over even your enemies, show courtesy, guard your good name, be kind to those in pain: this is how the good behave.
verse.why: Success should make you bow lower; real ornaments are listening, giving and helping.
verse.misuse: Winning over an enemy is not the same as tolerating harm.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On helping others
prasang.summary: Verses on generosity and friendship: trees bow with fruit, the hand shines by giving, a true friend keeps you from wrong and stays in trouble. Four kinds of people, from the selfless to those who harm for nothing.
prasang.lesson: Success should make you bow lower; real ornaments are listening, giving and helping.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari sits with you and says that true worth shows in how you treat the world. Success is not a crown that lifts you above others. It is the choice to bow lower. The real ornaments you wear are the quiet acts of listening, giving, and helping. Your good name is guarded not by loud claims, but by speaking truth and walking the path of the good. Even when you face those who do not value you, you meet them with patience and kindness. You do not win by tolerating harm.
verse.for_you: After work, when the children are not there, the quiet house waits. You do not need to fill it with noise to prove you are worthy. Let the television stay off for one evening. Just sit in the quiet and be kind to your own pain. That is the true ornament.

verse.speaker: Yudhishthira
verse.setting: At a poisoned lake, a Yaksha quizzes Yudhishthira; his brothers' lives hang on the answers.
verse.sanskrit: प्रियवचनवादी किं लभते / विमृशितकार्यकरः किं लभते / बहुमित्रकरः किं लभते / धर्मे रतः किं लभते कथय ॥ प्रियवचनवादी प्रियो भवति / विमृशितकार्यकरोऽधिकं जयति / बहुमित्रकरः सुखं वसति / यश्च धर्मरतः स गतिं लभते
verse.line: Speak kindly and you'll be loved; think before acting and you'll win more; make friends and live happily.
verse.translation: Yaksha: 'What does one gain by speaking kindly? By acting after careful thought? By making many friends? By devotion to what is right?' Yudhishthira: 'One who speaks kindly is loved; one who acts after careful thought wins more; one with many friends lives happily; one devoted to what is right reaches the goal.'
verse.why: Answer life's questions with a steady mind, and let kindness outweigh advantage.

prasang.title: Yaksha Prashna: the questions at the lake
prasang.summary: One by one, four Pandavas drink from a lake against a voice's warning and fall dead. Yudhishthira answers the Yaksha's riddles instead, and when offered one brother's life, chooses his stepmother's son Nakula, out of fairness.
prasang.story_hook: Four brothers lay dead by a clear lake, and the voice that killed them was asking Yudhishthira riddles.
prasang.lesson: Answer life's questions with a steady mind, and let kindness outweigh advantage.

verse.meaning: At the edge of a poisoned lake, a Yaksha asks Yudhishthira what life truly gains. The answer is not power or wealth. It is that speaking with kindness brings love, thinking before acting brings more, and living with many friends brings happiness. The lesson is to let kindness outweigh advantage, and to answer life's questions with a steady mind.
verse.for_you: The quiet house feels heavy right now. Let your words toward your children today be soft, even if you feel far away. Let your mind rest on what is true, not on what you think you failed to be.

story.title: Sumitra sits with Kausalya
story.story_hook: Two mothers, two sons gone to the same forest, and one of them found the strength to comfort the other.
story.summary: Kausalya weeps for her son gone to the forest. Her co-queen Sumitra, whose own son has gone too, comforts her: he went for a good reason, he is not alone, and you will see him again.
story.lesson: When a child leaves, a friend who shares the ache helps more than advice.

anchor.speaker: Sumitra
anchor.setting: Ram has left for fourteen years; his mother cannot stop weeping, and her co-queen sits with her.
anchor.sanskrit: निवृत्तवनवासं तं द्रष्टासि पुनरागतम्। जहि शोकं च मोहं च देवि सत्यं ब्रवीमि ते॥
anchor.line: You will see him again. Let go of this grief.
anchor.translation: You will see him again, back from the forest. Let go of grief and confusion, my queen. I tell you the truth.
anchor.why: When a child leaves, a friend who shares the ache helps more than advice.
anchor.misuse: Comfort for a long separation, not a promise that every loss will be undone.

prasang.story_hook: Two mothers, two sons gone to the same forest, and one of them found the strength to comfort the other.

story.hook_title: Both their sons were gone, and Sumitra found the strength to comfort Kausalya
story.teaser: Both their sons were gone, and Sumitra found the strength to comfort Kausalya
story.for_you: Sumitra knew the ache of a child gone. She did not fix the forest or the distance. She simply sat with Kausalya and said he would return. Let someone who knows your pain sit with you today, and let their presence be enough.

script: The quiet house is real, and it is heavy. You are keeping a secret from your parents in Chandigarh, and it is a weight that belongs to you alone right now.

Arjuna has collapsed on the battlefield. He looks at Krishna and says that even if he won everything, even the rule of the gods, it would not touch this grief. He is drying up inside. He admits he cannot see a way out. He asks Krishna to teach him what to do next. Arjuna said:
न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद्यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम्, अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धम्राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम्.
In plain words: Even winning everything wouldn't touch this grief that's drying me up inside.

Arjuna is saying that no amount of winning changes what is happening inside him. He is admitting he does not know the right thing to do. He is asking for help. This is where clarity begins, when you admit you do not know and ask for help. It is easier said than done, because we often feel we must have the answer before we reach out. But clarity does not come from having the answer. It comes from asking the question.

depth.life: You sit in the quiet house with the television on, carrying a secret from your parents. You are separated, seeing your children three nights a week, and you feel quietly lonely. You are not present with your kids, and your marriage feels distant.
depth.points: True clarity begins when you admit you do not know how to carry this. The texts say that even winning everything would not touch this grief. Your sorrow is real, and it will not be fixed by pretending it is not there.
depth.practice: Name the sorrow you feel right now, out loud, to yourself. Say it is real and it is not your size.
depth.question: What would it feel like to admit you do not know how to carry this alone?
